context.exploration_scope: Final verification that the S22->S23 Trigger->Response loop is structurally sound end-to-end: confirmed unbroken S21->S22->S23 checkpoint provenance, mechanically validated all 4 historical trigger records' causal shape, compared LIVE state against the S23 checkpoint, and re-confirmed no existing Principle/Decision record was modified

problem: S22 and S23 each individually demonstrated the change-gated trigger working correctly on their own run, but neither phase verified that the OTHER phase's checkpoint was genuinely inherited rather than independently reconstructed to happen to match, nor that the recorded verdict fields would be structurally self-consistent if a comparison ever were performed -- closing the loop required an independent, mechanical audit of the whole S21->S22->S23 chain plus one more live comparison, not just trusting that two individually-correct phases compose correctly.

action.action_summary: Deep-equality-verified the S21->S22->S23 checkpoint provenance chain for both Principles; mechanically validated the Trigger->Independent Judgment->Principle Judgment->Outcome causal shape of all 4 historical trigger records; compared LIVE real state against the S23 checkpoint per Principle, executing a judgment loop only where a real change was found; re-confirmed byte-identical S4/S18 Principle adoption records and the S6 Principle-guided Decision record.

result.note: The full S21->S22->S23 checkpoint chain traced cleanly, all 4 historical trigger records were structurally self-consistent, the live-vs-checkpoint gate correctly ran no judgment loop this run (real data unchanged), and no existing Principle or Decision record was touched -- the operational loop is demonstrably closed, still not CI/policy/execution-wired.

cause.root_cause_summary: Two phases that each individually behave correctly can still silently drift apart if the second one is allowed to reconstruct a value that merely happens to equal what the first one recorded, rather than being required to literally inherit it -- checkpoint provenance and trigger-record shape both need their own explicit, mechanical audit, separate from each individual phase's own internal correctness, before the multi-phase loop as a whole can be called closed.

lesson: Closing a multi-phase operational loop is a distinct claim from any one phase in it being correct -- it requires deep-equality-verifying that each phase's stated checkpoint literally traces back through the prior phase's own recorded output (not an independently-reconstructed lookalike), and mechanically validating that every trigger record's causal fields (independent verdict, Principle-guided verdict, match, result) are internally consistent wherever a comparison actually ran, and correctly empty wherever it did not.
